title: Work with coordinate frames
scope: SE(2), labelled transforms and point/direction semantics

items.prompt: Column vectors: T_AB maps B coordinates into A. Which transform maps B into A? Return T_AB or T_BA.
items.solution: The first subscript is the destination frame; the second is the source. Reverse direction uses the inverse.

items.prompt: Column vectors, T_AB maps B→A: T_AB is +π/2 rotation with translation (1,2); T_BC is pure translation (3,−1). Find the translation of T_AC=T_AB T_BC.
items.solution: Rotate (3,−1) to (1,3) then add (1,2): (2,5). Reversing order is not equivalent.

items.prompt: T_WS maps shelf coordinates S into warehouse W. To express a warehouse point in shelf coordinates, choose T_WS or inverse(T_WS). Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: The coordinate destination is shelf S. Reverse the map using its inverse; do not merely rename the point.

items.prompt: A shelf transform rotates −π/2 and then translates (5,-2) m. Map point (1,2) and direction (1,2), returning point x,y then direction x,y. Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: A clockwise quarter-turn maps (1,2) to (2,−1). Add the offset to the point only.

items.prompt: T_WS=[[cos θ,−sin θ,3],[sin θ,cos θ,-2],[0,0,1]], θ=0.6000000000000001 rad. Return the complete 3×3 inverse T_SW, row by row. Units: metres and radians. Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: Transpose R and use inverse offset −R^T p. The bottom row stays (0,0,1). A plain negated translation is generally wrong.

items.prompt: An estimated 2×2 map is R=[[0, -1], [1, 0]]. Is it a proper planar rotation? Both orthonormal columns and determinant +1 are required. Return yes or no. Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: A determinant of +1 alone is insufficient. A shear changes lengths; a quarter-turn preserves lengths and orientation.
